summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reported that articles for the Allen-Ben Hogan fight would be signed at Looney & Herbert's Sixth Street saloon, and that Mike Ganley called the McCoole fight the most one-sided he had ever seen.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Thursday, September 25, 1873'; not the Globe-Democrat until 1875.

facts.fact: Articles for a fight between Allen and Ben Hogan were to be signed at 3 o'clock at Looney & Herbert's Sixth Street saloon in St. Louis, arranged by Mike Ganley
places: Looney & Herbert's saloon, Sixth Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Mike Ganley stood ready to back Joe Coburn against Allen

notes: The headline says the signing is 'to-day' but the text says 'to-morrow'; 473 shows it took place September 25. Also mentions Allen's benefit at the Theater Comique that night (see 471) and the Democrat's scoop on the McCoole fight result.
